messages:
sarah: Seeing a sharp spike in NVMe read latency in ap-southeast1 — attach timeouts for GPU provisioning (~30 failed attaches over 7m). This started right after the control-plane firmware push. Anyone tracking?

ops-oncall: Looking now. Provisioning dashboard shows attach_errors + i/o timeouts. Can you paste the error? :eyes:

storage-bot: ALERT: nvme.controller.reset rate increased from 0.01/s -> 0.9/s across nodes gnode-120..gnode-142 in ap-southeast1 between 12:15-12:22 UTC. Implicated service: gpu-pool-ephemeral.

matt: Yep, also seeing janitor scrub jobs spike during the same window. Heavy scrub + attach heavy IO could cause head-of-line blocking on the NVMe scheduler.

anya: We can throttle scrubs temporarily. Recommend setting janitor.scrub.max-iops to 100 for the region while we triage. Ops, can you roll that to canaries?

ops-oncall: Doing canary now — annotating 3 nodes to pick up the lower scrub cap. Command I'm running: 
```
kubectl -n infra annotate node gnode-120 janitor.scrub-max-iops=100 --overwrite
kubectl -n infra annotate node gnode-125 janitor.scrub-max-iops=100 --overwrite
kubectl -n infra annotate node gnode-130 janitor.scrub-max-iops=100 --overwrite
```

rahul: FWIW firmware release notes show a regression between 2.1.4 -> 2.1.5 that can increase controller reset frequency under concurrent heavy IO. We should pause the firmware rollout until we confirm.

sarah: Any sign of metadata/block corruption? Scrub logs earlier showed a couple checksum mismatches but nodes auto-remounted readonly then recovered. Not seeing widespread corruption yet.

storage-bot: DETECTED: 2 checksum errors logged. gnode-135: block_checksum_mismatch on /dev/nvme0n1, gnode-139: transient crc error. No blockmap loss detected. Short log snippet:
```
[12:17:02] nvme0n1: read error LBA 0x1f4a2 (retrying)
[12:17:03] nvme0n1: controller reset (code 0x5)
[12:17:04] janitor: checksum_mismatch: obj=tmpfile-87fd
```

matt: Proposed immediate plan: 1) throttle janitor scrubs in ap-southeast1 (in flight) 2) pause firmware rollout for remaining nodes in region 3) mark nodes with >0.5 resets/min as drain candidates 4) failover GPU provisioning to us-west for new requests until attach success >95% in region.

anya: Agree. Cost note: traffic -> us-west will bump egress and spot prices ~12% for the next 4h; also increased latency for serving customers in APAC. Are SLO owners OK? @julia-finance FYI on cost hit.

julia-finance: acknowledged — temporary cost delta acceptable for incident mitigation. Please keep to the 4h window if possible.

ops-oncall: Actions executed: annotated canaries (throttle), paused firmware rollout in ap-southeast1, marked 8 nodes as drain-candidate (automated drain kicks in). Updated routing policy to prefer us-west for new GPU attaches where attach_latency > 1s. Observability will report in ~5m. :white_check_mark:

mike: Observability update: canaries improved — attach success rate climbed from 72% -> 95% on annotated nodes, nvme.controller.reset dropped to 0.12/s. We'll keep the region under watch for 2h and roll back the scrub throttle only after stable metrics for 30m.

sarah: Thanks team. Keeping oncall until metrics are stable. I'll open a postmortem ticket to decide longer-term fixes: staggered scrub windows by zone, firmware rollout gating by controller-reset metric, and explicit provisioning fallback across regions.

matt: Also add a tracking item: consider per-node NVMe QoS (io_uring/blk-mq tweaks) to prevent scrubs from starving attach path.

anya: Noted. If anyone sees new checksum/corruption hits, flag immediately and stop autoscale attach in that cell.

sarah: Closing thread for now; will post updates in the incident doc. Thanks everyone. :pray:
